title: Blackcurrant frangipane tart
subtitle: almond cream tart with sharp blackcurrants pressed into the filling
excerpt: Blackcurrant frangipane tart uses the same method as the fig version but with British blackcurrants, which have a sharp, intensely fruity flavour that cuts through the sweetness of the almond cream. Blackcurrants are pressed into the raw frangipane before baking; they sink and burst, giving a jewelled, jammy filling. Fresh or frozen blackcurrants both work.
sourceNotes: Blackcurrant frangipane tart, a British summer seasonal tart using native blackcurrants. Method from standard British patisserie practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A filling made from ground almonds, butter, sugar, and eggs. It swells and sets during baking to a soft, moist almond cream.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The pastry case can be blind-baked up to 2 days ahead. Fill and bake on the day of serving.

content.text: is made in the same way for any frangipane tart: creamed butter and sugar, eggs, ground almonds. The blackcurrants are scattered over the surface of the raw frangipane and pressed in slightly. They sink during baking, creating pockets of purple juice through the filling. If using frozen blackcurrants, scatter them frozen directly onto the filling: no need to defrost.

Rub the cold butter into the flour and icing sugar to fine crumbs. Stir in the egg yolk and enough cold water (1 to 2 tablespoons) to bring the dough together. Refrigerate for 30 minutes, then roll out and line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin. Refrigerate for a further 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan. Blind-bake for 15 minutes, remove the beans and bake for a further 5 minutes. Set aside.
Beat the butter and caster sugar until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the ground almonds.
Spread the frangipane in the pastry case. Scatter the blackcurrants over the surface and press them in lightly so they are just below the surface.

Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the frangipane is set and golden and a skewer inserted between the fruit comes out clean. The filling will puff and then settle as it cools. Cool in the tin for 20 minutes before removing. Dust with icing sugar to serve.

attrs.problem: Frangipane filling liquid in the centre
attrs.avoid: Avoid opening the oven before 25 minutes; the filling needs to cook from the outside in.
attrs.fix: Return to the oven for 5 to 10 more minutes. Cover the edges of the pastry with foil if they are browning too fast.

attrs.problem: Pastry case shrinking and sides collapsing during blind-baking
attrs.avoid: Avoid rolling the pastry too thin or skipping the chilling time after lining the tin.
attrs.fix: Refrigerate the lined tin for at least 30 minutes before blind-baking; cold pastry holds its shape.
